mem.7:
May 8, 2023 — Caroline and Melanie (“Mel”) caught up. Mel was busy with work and children. Caroline had attended an LGBTQ support group the day before; hearing trans people’s stories made her feel accepted, supported, and more courageous about embracing herself. She planned to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health careers to help people with similar experiences. Mel said she’d make a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall painted with a woman; Mel liked the painting. Mel shared her 2022 painting of a sunrise over a lake, which she valued for self-expression, creativity, and relaxation. Caroline praised the colors. Caroline left to research; Mel went swimming with her kids.

May 25, 2023 — Mel said she had run a mental-health charity race on May 20. It made her reflect on well-being and self-care; she was trying to make daily time for running, reading, or violin, though self-care remained a work in progress. Her kids were excited for summer; family was considering camping in June. Caroline was researching adoption agencies. Having a family and giving children in need a loving home had long been her dream. She shared a photo of an adoption-agency sign/building. She chose the agency because it supports LGBTQ+ adopters and felt hopeful, though she had much to learn. She looked forward to creating a family, while aware single parenting would be challenging. Mel said she’d be an awesome mom; Caroline hoped to offer a safe, loving home, and Mel felt she would provide love and stability.

June 9, 2023 — Caroline described speaking at a school event the previous week about her transgender journey and encouraging student involvement in the LGBTQ community. She felt powerful sharing struggles, coming out, and personal growth; audience members related and were inspired to be better allies. She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion promote understanding, acceptance, and hope. Caroline began transitioning around 2020. Mel praised her courage and advocacy. Caroline called friends, family, and mentors her “rocks”; she had known her support-network friends for four years, since moving from her home country around 2019. Their support was especially important after a difficult breakup. Caroline shared a family/friends photo in a yard. Mel said her husband and children motivate and support her; she and her husband had been married five years (since around 2018). She shared a photo of a man and little girl in front of a waterfall and a wedding photo of herself in a dress holding a bouquet. Caroline congratulated her. Mel also shared a family picnic photo (man and woman sitting on a blanket eating); she treasured the games, food, and time together, which made her feel alive and happy. Caroline agreed that time with loved ones brings gratitude and happiness; family is everything.

June 27, 2023 — Caroline shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and heart, a childhood gift from her grandmother in Sweden. It represents love, faith, and strength, and reminds her of her roots and family’s support. Mel shared patterned bowls and asked about treasured objects. Caroline’s friend had made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, ten years earlier (around 2013); its design and colors remind her of art and self-expression. Mel said she had taken her family camping in the mountains the previous week (around June 20): nature walks, hiking, campfire marshmallows, and an amazing summit view. Her two younger children love nature; she treasured the trip. Caroline was glad they made memories.

Caroline remained interested in counseling/mental-health work, possibly supporting trans people’s self-acceptance and mental health. She shared a bookshelf photo and described attending an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on Friday, June 23, about therapeutic approaches and working effectively with trans people. It was enlightening; professionals’ dedication to safe spaces inspired her. Counseling and support groups had helped her own journey and motivated her to create a welcoming place for others. Mel encouraged her and also shared a photo of a bookshelf in a room.

July 3, 2023 — Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the previous week. Its joyful atmosphere made her feel she belonged and showed how much the community had grown. It motivated her to use her story to help others; she remained excited about counseling/mental-health work. Mel had signed up for a pottery class the day before; she found pottery therapeutic, creative, and expressive. She shared a photo of someone holding a frisbee and one of a bowl she made, decorated with a black-and-white flower. She was proud of it and said pottery was important in her life, helping her express emotions and bringing joy. Caroline praised her creativity and said she was learning piano. Caroline planned to attend a transgender conference in July to meet people and learn about advocacy; Mel wished her fun and safety.

July 6, 2023 — Caroline had been looking further into counseling/mental-health work; helping people and making a positive impact felt challenging but rewarding. Mel said she took her kids to a museum on July 5 and shared a photo of two children playing in a water-play area. They especially enjoyed the dinosaur exhibit, learning about animals, and seeing bones; it reminded Mel why she loves being a mom. Caroline said motherhood was awesome and she was building a library for her future children, with children’s classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. She shared a bookcase photo and looked forward to reading with them. Mel’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*; friendship and compassion meant a lot to her. She shared a photo of a cover showing a girl and cat. Caroline said those themes made her appreciate friends and family who helped her through transition. Caroline had picnicked with friends the previous week and shared a photo of women sitting on a blanket in a park. Her support network gave love, guidance, and acceptance throughout her transition; their unconditional encouragement helped her accept and grow into her true self, and she couldn’t have done it without them. Mel also shared a photo of her family camping at a beach campfire; they love it and feel closer together.

July 12, 2023 — Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ conference on July 10. Meeting people with similar journeys in a welcoming environment made her feel accepted and grateful for the community. It reinforced the importance of fighting for trans rights and spreading awareness. She noted progress but said more was needed and wanted to help. She was still looking into counseling and mental-health jobs so people would have someone to talk to. Her own mental-health struggles and helpful support had motivated her to help others on similar journeys. Mel praised her and shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin; a book she read the previous year reminded her to pursue dreams. Caroline said books guide and motivate her and help her discover herself. Her favorite was *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family; it made Caroline feel connected and hopeful. She shared a photo of a dog in a boat on the water. The book taught her self-acceptance, finding support, and that hard times don’t last; hope and love exist. They agreed pets bring joy and comfort. Mel shared photos of two little girls on steps with a dog and a cat lying on the floor. Her family has a dog and cat named Luna and Oliver; they are sweet, playful, and brighten the house. Mel also shared pink sneakers (Caroline called the color purple); they were running shoes. Mel had been running farther since the prior chat to destress and clear her mind, improving her mental health, and planned to continue. She had shared photos of the shoes being worn and in a box. Caroline encouraged her and emphasized self-care and mental health.
mem.13:
Caroline and Melanie are close friends/supporters. Caroline says Melanie helps her notice happy moments; Melanie says Caroline makes struggles bearable. They attended a Pride festival together in 2022 and fondly remember it. On 17 Aug 2023 they agreed to plan a summer outing, perhaps catching up and exploring nature.

**Caroline:** Trans woman from Sweden; surname unknown. Had been transitioning for three years by 9 Jun 2023. Friends she knew since moving from Sweden, family and mentors supported her through transition and a difficult breakup; their love and acceptance helped her grow into herself. A cross-and-heart necklace her Swedish grandmother gave her as a child represents love, faith, strength, roots and family support. A friend gave her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, about 2013; its colors/pattern evoke art and self-expression. Blue is her favorite color and relaxes her.

Counseling and LGBTQ support groups helped her mental health and self-understanding. At a group on 7 May 2023 she felt accepted and inspired by trans stories. She attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop on 23 Jun, learning therapeutic methods and about working with trans people; she valued professionals’ commitment to safe spaces. She hopes to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health work, especially supporting trans people and helping them accept themselves. She wants to create welcoming spaces and be someone others can talk to.

She attended Pride events/parades in late June/early July and on 11 Aug 2023; they brought belonging, happiness, pride and gratitude and strengthened her commitment to trans rights, equality, awareness and inclusion. At an LGBTQ conference on 10 Jul she met people with similar experiences and felt welcomed. The week before 9 Jun she gave a school talk about her journey, struggles and growth since coming out; students related, were encouraged to be better allies and responded positively. She wants her story to foster understanding and lift others up. She joined Connected LGBTQ Activists on 18 Jul; members plan campaigns/events and support one another. She finds it fulfilling and a platform for advocacy. She missed her city’s Pride parade on 15–16 Jul, but it reminded her people are not alone. On a hike, conservative religious comments upset her (17 Aug); supportive people helped her feel she would be okay.

Caroline’s longstanding dream is to become a single parent and give children a safe, loving home. She researches adoption and by 25 May 2023 was considering an LGBTQ-inclusive agency. A 14 Jul council meeting strengthened her resolve. She is hopeful and feels ready despite knowing it will be hard; friends and mentors support her. She collects children’s books for a future library: classics, books from different cultures and educational books. She loves books as guidance; favorite is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, an inspiring true story that gave her connection and hope, teaching self-acceptance, support and that hard times pass. A book-cover photo Melanie shared on 12 Jul reminded her to keep going. She says pets bring joy.

Caroline uses art to explore transition, her changing body and self-acceptance, including embracing imperfections; she values inclusive representation and telling her trans story through art. “Embracing Identity” shows a woman becoming comfortable and loving herself. She planned an LGBTQ art show for Aug 2023; a tree and bright sun painting inspired by an LGBTQ center represents unity and strength. On the weekend of 15–16 Jul she joined LGBTQ youth mentorship, mentoring a trans teen; she finds it rewarding and says it is going well. They attended a June Pride event; the teen’s face lit up at the love and acceptance. On 23 Aug 2023 Caroline said she applied to adoption agencies that week after attending an adoption advice/assistance group. She felt excited but nervous about parenting’s responsibility. Her guinea pig is Oscar; he likes vegetables, especially parsley. She loved horseback riding with her father as a child, riding through fields and feeling the wind; she has always loved horses. A self-portrait with a blue face, painted the week before 23 Aug, made her feel liberated and empowered; art helps her explore identity, be true to herself and is therapeutic. Supportive people, promoting LGBTQ rights and living authentically also give her freedom; she wants others to live authentically.

**Melanie:** Surname unknown. Married about 2018; had been married five years by 9 Jun 2023. Husband and children motivate her; she wants courage for her family. Cherishes time with loved ones. Wedding photo showed bride holding flowers; she recalls a loving, joyful ceremony with loved ones and treasured promising forever to her partner. Flowers evoke joy, growth, beauty, small moments and wedding decor. Photos showed a family picnic/outdoor meal and a man with a little girl at a waterfall; identities unconfirmed. Family games, good food and outings bring joy. Her family helped her through a move with practical help and love.

Has children, including a youngest daughter; her first steps reminded Melanie life is fleeting. Took children swimming (8 May 2023), to a museum (5 Jul; they loved dinosaurs, animals and bones) and pottery workshop (14 Jul; they made clay sculptures including a dog-face cup). They paint nature scenes together; on 8–9 Jul they painted a sunset with a palm tree and talked about nature. Children were excited for summer break; camping in June was considered. Family enjoys camping, mountain hikes, forests and beach camping. In the week before 27 Jun they camped in mountains, hiked, explored, roasted marshmallows and admired the summit view; younger children love nature. Camped 1–2 Jul; Melanie enjoyed unplugging. They look forward to campfires, stories and marshmallows. On a 2022 camping trip they watched the Perseid meteor shower, made wishes beneath a clear sky and felt one with the universe. They go to the beach once or twice yearly; a recent visit with children, and seeing them happy, was especially enjoyable. On 13 Aug 2023 she celebrated her daughter’s birthday with her children at a Matt Patterson concert; she loved his voice and songs.

Melanie values self-care, still a work in progress; it helps her care for family. Daily activities include running, reading and violin. After a mental-health charity race on 20 May 2023 she reflected on mental-health care. By 12 Jul she was running longer/farther to de-stress and clear her mind, improving her mental health. She painted a lake sunrise in 2022; painting helps express feelings, relax and create. Pottery is a major part of her life, not just a hobby: clay is calming, joyful, expressive and a sanctuary. Signed up for pottery on 2 Jul; made a black-and-white flower bowl and was proud. On 17 Aug she showed Caroline a colorful bowl designed to catch the eye and make people smile. Art brings comfort, happiness, fulfillment and learning. She has pets Luna and Oliver (which is the dog vs. cat unspecified); both playful and sweet. Favorite childhood book: *Charlotte’s Web*, for friendship and compassion.

On 23 Aug 2023 Melanie said her pets were well and she had recently added a cat named Bailey; she showed Caroline a photo described as Oliver, a black dog lying in grass with a frisbee. Oliver once hid his bone in her slipper. Melanie had fed a horse a carrot and painted a horse on a wooden wall; she loves painting animals, finding it peaceful and special, and admires horses’ grace. Both friends wished Caroline well on adoption; Melanie offered ongoing support.
mem.19:
Caroline and Melanie (surnames unknown) are close friends and supporters. Caroline says Melanie helps her notice happy moments; Melanie says Caroline makes struggles bearable. They attended Pride in 2022 and planned a summer outing for 17 Aug 2023.

Caroline is a Swedish trans woman; by 9 Jun 2023 she’d been transitioning three years. Friends, family and mentors supported her through transition and a difficult breakup. Her grandmother’s cross-and-heart necklace symbolizes love, faith, strength, roots and family support. A friend’s hand-painted bowl was an 18th-birthday gift (c. 2013), tied to art and self-expression. Favorite color is relaxing blue. Counseling and LGBTQ groups helped her mental health and self-understanding. She hopes to work/study in counseling and create welcoming spaces. LGBTQ gatherings, a 10 Jul conference, and speaking at school the week before 9 Jun gave her belonging and strengthened her commitment to equality. Joined Connected LGBTQ Activists 18 Jul. Missed city Pride 15–16 Jul but felt reassured people aren’t alone. Conservative religious remarks upset her on a hike 17 Aug; by 25 Aug she said loving trans community made a huge difference.

Caroline dreams of single parenthood and a safe, loving home. Researched adoption by 25 May; considered LGBTQ-inclusive agency. Council meeting 14 Jul strengthened resolve. On 23 Aug said she’d applied to agencies that week after group advice/help; excited and nervous. On 13 Oct asked mentor for advice, feeling ready to be a mom. On 22 Oct she passed adoption agency interviews the prior Friday, a major step. Wants to give children without a home love, acceptance and support; sees adoption as giving back. Collects children’s books for future library; favorite *Becoming Nicole* (Amy Ellis Nutt), about connection, hope and self-acceptance; Melanie sent its cover 12 Jul. Guinea pig Oscar likes parsley; Caroline loved childhood horseback riding with her father.

Caroline’s art explores transition, body, imperfection, identity and self-acceptance; “Embracing Identity” is about self-love. Planned LGBTQ art show for Aug, prepared September show. Tree/sun painting inspired by LGBTQ center symbolizes unity/strength. Mentored trans teen 15–16 Jul; teen felt accepted at June Pride. Blue-faced self-portrait before 23 Aug felt liberating. Church stained glass (25 Aug) depicts time and her trans journey; another window’s key symbolizes potential. Wants art celebrating difference/togetherness. Rainbow sidewalk lifted her mood; flowers capture feelings; beach sunset painting was calming. On 13 Sep shared heart painting about community; making art since c. 17, empowering/cathartic. Red/blue painting represents gender binary; mixed colors reject rigid thinking. Some friends supported transition, others couldn’t; accepting relationships feel more genuine. Considered pottery. Volunteered at LGBTQ+ youth center by 28 Aug, found guiding youth fulfilling; center planned September kids’ talent show. Plays acoustic guitar since c. 2018; Sara Bareilles’ “Brave” reminds her of courage/progress.

Melanie married c. 2018; five years married by 9 Jun 2023. Husband and children motivate her; family time, games, meals and outings bring joy. Youngest daughter’s first steps reminded her life is fleeting; family helped during a move. Activities include swimming, museums, pottery, painting with kids, camping and hiking. Kids loved dinosaurs/animals/bones at 5 Jul museum. Pottery workshop 14 Jul; dog-face cup. Loves forests, mountains and beach camping. Mountain outing week before 27 Jun included marshmallows and summit views; camped 1–2 Jul, enjoying unplugging, fires and stories. Watched Perseids camping in 2022 and made wishes. Family beach trips once/twice yearly. On 13 Aug celebrated daughter’s birthday at Matt Patterson concert; liked his voice/songs.

Melanie values self-care, still a work in progress. Runs, reads, plays violin; ran mental-health charity race 20 May and farther to de-stress by 12 Jul. Painting expresses feelings/relaxes; painted lake sunrise in 2022. Pottery is calming sanctuary/major part of life; signed up 2 Jul, made black-and-white flower bowl and felt proud; shared colorful bowl 17 Aug to catch eyes/make people smile. Childhood favorite *Charlotte’s Web* (friendship/compassion). Pets Luna, Oliver and, by 23 Aug, cat Bailey. Oliver is a black dog, likes frisbee, once hid a bone in a slipper. Melanie admires horses’ grace; fed one a carrot and painted one on a wooden wall. Plays clarinet since young; likes Bach, Mozart, Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect” and live music.

25 Aug: Caroline discussed upsetting hike and apology; mountaintop photo. Melanie showed pottery plate decorated with flowers, made previous day, and discussed meaningful family volunteering at homeless shelter. They discussed rainbow-flag crowd, trans community, mural (courage/strength), eagle (freedom/pride/resilience), stained glass, sidewalk and flower art. Melanie likes landscape/still life; sunflower recently, autumn works planned; supports LGBTQ art platforms.
28 Aug: Melanie took kids to park; shared playground and stage/band photos; “Summer Sounds” played energetic pop. Shared piano drawing/sheet music/pencil photos and unspecified laptop/graph photo.
13 Sep: Caroline’s group biked prior weekend; beach/fence/sunset photo, refreshing day. Melanie shared yellow-leaved forest road; family had camped weeks earlier, hiked, roasted marshmallows, told stories. She’d painted/potted for seven years; shared bowls and starfish. Caroline shared painting about trans journey; Melanie expressed pride. Melanie shared café visit and door sign saying someone was “not being able to leave”; precaution only, nothing happened. Caroline checked in; Melanie appreciated it, later called it fun park time.
13 Oct: Melanie had been injured in Sep and paused pottery; reading Caroline’s recommended book and painting. Shared calming pink-sky sunset. Caroline tried abstract art for emotional freedom; Melanie shared abstract wall painting, blue streaks symbolizing tranquility. Caroline attended transgender poetry reading the previous Friday; powerful, safe, empowering. Shared classroom poster and “Trans Lives Matter” sign; supportive room and pride/strength posters inspired art. Drawing of woman in dress symbolizes freedom, authenticity, womanhood. Both affirmed being true to themselves and learning together.
20 Oct: Melanie’s road trip the previous weekend was frightening: son was in a car accident but okay. Dashboard photo with white cloth/steering wheel. Accident made her value family and life; children scared but reassured, resilient, give her strength. Shared photo of two children overlooking Grand Canyon; they enjoyed it. Woman and child walking trail photo taken 19 Oct, relaxing outing after trip. Loves camping together, stories/campfires/nature, waking to birds and fresh air; shared sunset over water. Nature resets and refreshes her.
22 Oct: Caroline shared passing adoption agency interviews, excited and thankful. Melanie shared photo of two wooden dolls on a table, bought 21 Oct, reminding her of family love, and asked Caroline’s future vision. Caroline spoke of building a family, giving children a roof and a safe, loving home; adoption is love, acceptance and giving back. She said self-acceptance was long and transition difficult, but support from friends, family and mentors helped her find herself; she wants to pass that support on. Melanie praised her strength and inspiration; they affirmed mutual support and being oneself. Caroline shared a green/yellow-designed clock and a painting with “happiness” written on it.
